chapter_title: Improving a Resource with AI Agents
learning_objective: The learner will judge each of six AI-drafted alt texts as accept, correct, or reject, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** ai-alt-text-reviewer
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge each of six AI-drafted alt texts as accept, correct, or reject, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** AI Alt Text Generation, Accept Correct or Reject, Hallucination, and the alt text sections of Chapter 7 (all defined in this chapter above this block or in earlier chapters). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each draft the learner commits one of three decisions. A decision is correct when it matches the Correct decision column in Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Reading the decision definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A fluent description is a correct one. (2) Every image needs alt text with words. (3) A draft that is almost right should be thrown away. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging a draft against the image and its lesson context is an Evaluate-level action. Drafts that are accurate, generic, wrongly detailed, and invented teach the learner to compare each draft with what the image shows and what the lesson needs. **Content:** The three decisions: Accept (accurate and useful as written), Correct (right in substance, with a detail or purpose to fix), Reject (describes something that is not in the image). The six items (all made up). Each shows a plain description of what the image contains, the lesson sentence beside it, and the agent's draft: | # | What the image contains | Lesson sentence | Agent draft | Correct decision | Corrected text shown after | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | A photo of the Clearwater River in a wide bend, seen from a bridge. | Rivers on flat land bend back and forth in curves called meanders. | A photo of a river. | Correct | The Clearwater River curving in a wide bend, seen from a bridge. | The draft is generic and misses the bend that the lesson is about. | | 2 | A bar chart of monthly river flow, highest in April and lowest in September. | River flow is highest in spring. | Bar chart of monthly river flow, highest in April and lowest in September. | Accept | None | The draft is accurate and short. The chart still needs a data table nearby. | | 3 | A thin decorative wave line between two sections. | None | Blue wave line separating two sections. | Correct | Empty alt text | A decorative image should have empty alt text so that a screen reader skips it. | | 4 | A diagram of the water cycle with arrows from the ocean to a cloud to a mountain to a river. | Water moves in a cycle between the sea, the air, and the land. | A satellite photo of a city at night. | Reject | A diagram of the water cycle, with arrows from the ocean to a cloud, to a mountain, and to a river. | The draft describes something that is not in the image. | | 5 | A photo of two students measuring the depth of a stream with a ruler. | Students measure the depth of the stream. | Two students use a ruler to measure the depth of a stream. | Accept | None | The draft matches the image and the lesson. | | 6 | A map of the river with two tributaries. | The map shows how the tributaries join the river. | Map showing the river and its three tributaries. | Correct | Map showing the river and its two tributaries. | The draft is right in substance and the count is wrong. | **Provenance:** The images and drafts are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The decisions follow Chapter 14 and the alt text rules of Chapter 7. **Rules:** Each item has exactly one correct decision. Two are Accept, three are Correct, and one is Reject. The sim shows each image as a plain description of its contents. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the image description, the lesson sentence, and the agent's draft. 2. The learner chooses a decision, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct, the corrected text when there is one, and the Why text. 4. After item 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 items in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [decision]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The decision is [decision]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can review an agent's alt text." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed item. **Starting State:** The first item in the shuffled order and the three decisions. The question shown is "What should the reviewer do with this draft?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists four mistakes in agent alt text: generic text, details not in the image, wrong counts or labels, and a missing decorative role. Items 1, 4, 6, and 3 show them in that order.
